idiom_name: sealed message hierarchy + exhaustive when expression
implementation_notes: Kotlin's sealed classes and interfaces give a message set closed at compile time, and when over that hierarchy is checked for exhaustiveness by the compiler (no else branch required, verified), so the routing table *is* the type hierarchy: the classic router object and its condition list disappear, and a new message type is a build error until it is routed. Where the discriminator arrives as a value on the wire, decode to the sealed type first (kotlinx.serialization polymorphic support) and route on the type; a when over a String is not exhaustive and still needs its else branch. A JVM integration stack (Spring Integration @Router, Camel choice) stays available and is the right choice when routes are configuration rather than code.
pitfalls: Only sealed hierarchies are checked: routing on msg.kind (a String) compiles without an else and silently does nothing for an unknown value, so decode to the sealed type first.
Sealed subclasses must live in the same package and module (verified), so a message type defined elsewhere cannot join the hierarchy - the guarantee and the limitation are the same fact.
A suspending send inside when makes the router a suspend function, and a blocking call (JDBC, file IO) in an arm stalls the coroutine dispatcher for every route it serves.
